correctness.rationale: For each integer degree l>=1, normalized angular-order eigenvalues are exact Legendre-square cap integrals. An order-raising identity plus the associated Legendre differential equation give an explicit integrated boundary Wronskian B(c), whose factorial normalization produces the claimed positive-factor product. Derivative Legendre polynomials have all roots simple in (-1,1) by Rolle and degree count, giving exactly l-m-1 simple positive-root crossings for each adjacent pair. Simultaneous vanishing of the two neighboring products forces the shared middle derivative zero: the alternative would force a polynomial and its derivative to vanish at one positive point through the differentiated Legendre ODE. The same reasoning excludes four consecutive equal levels. Parity and endpoint expansions give the unique lead m=l-1 near a hemisphere and m=0 near a point cap. The embedded exact symbolic checker tests 330 assertion groups for degrees 1..11; these are corroboration only. All claims exclude c=0 and c=1; nonconsecutive coincidences are unproved.

value.rationale: The spherical-cap concentration operator is a canonical spectral-localization object. General low-pass Slepian solvers and the hemisphere half-energy law do not quantify how exact angular-momentum sectors exchange concentration when cap radius changes. The theorem supplies a complete all-degree count of spectral crossings and of triple simultaneous level resonances, proves that consecutive fourfold equality is impossible, and detects a forced change of the optimal angular mode between geometric endpoints. The nontrivial count holds for a natural complete exact-degree family and is not a chosen single parameter, routine normalization, or finite experiment. The theorem makes no unsupported claim about arbitrary Slepian bands.
